system_description.narrative_title: Multipolar turbulence: wars, energy flows, and techno-diplomatic friction
system_description.narrative_summary: The global geopolitical order is an open, multipolar system in flux where overlapping regional wars (Ukraine, Iran/Gulf, Yemen), shifting sanctions and energy flows, and contested diplomacy among the US, Europe, and Russia interact. Domestic political turns in major powers and emergent domains—cyber, space communications, and disinformation—are changing battlefield dynamics and alliance cohesion. Feedbacks among energy markets, maritime security, coalition bargaining, and technological disruption are amplifying uncertainty for states, markets, and populations.
system_description.scope: Interstate and proxy conflicts (Ukraine, Iran-Gulf, Yemen), global energy markets and shipping routes, sanctions and financial channels, diplomacy and alliance politics (US, EU, Russia, regional actors), strategic technologies (space communications, cyber, deepfakes), and associated humanitarian and market impacts.
system_description.super_system: The global political-economic system (the international order embedded within the globalized economy and planetary security environment).
adjacent_subsystems: Global energy markets and commodity trading
Middle East–Gulf security and maritime chokepoints
Technology and information-warfare domain (cyber, space comms, disinformation)

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine war
variables.description: Russia's large-scale war against Ukraine, sustained Western military and economic support, and grinding battlefield attrition are reshaping European security and deterrence calculations.

variables.name: Iran–Gulf escalation
variables.description: Iran, its regional proxies and Gulf states (with U.S. involvement) are engaged in a widening campaign of missile, mine and Houthi attacks that is militarizing maritime routes and raising the risk of wider confrontation.

variables.name: Global oil market rebalancing
variables.description: A rapid recovery of shipments from Gulf producers, flows from alternative suppliers and shifting refinery/diesel dynamics have swung markets toward a crude surplus, altering revenues and leverage across producer and consumer states.

variables.name: Strategic communications and cyber warfare
variables.description: States and private actors are contesting command of networks and narratives — via satellite access controls, deepfakes, cyberattacks and other information-operations — changing battlefield command, intelligence access and political messaging.

variables.name: Transatlantic alliance cohesion
variables.description: Tensions over defense funding, industrial projects, how (or whether) to engage with Moscow, and divergent U.S. policy signals are stressing NATO/EU unity and burden-sharing arrangements.
